title: Identity for AI Agents - Patrick Riley & Carlos Galan, Auth0
talk_summary: An Auth0 workshop demoing OAuth-based identity for AI agents: token vault for upstream refresh tokens, async CIBA-style human approval for risky actions, and MCP server authorization via DCR/PKCE.

takeaways.what_they_do: Tool authorization is performed by deterministic SDK code before tool execution; the model never requests or mints scopes, and unrecognized scopes are dropped.

Risky operations (e.g. placing an order) block on an out-of-band approval request carrying structured details; the agent resumes only after approval returns a token scoped to exactly what was approved.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't want an hallucinating agent buying a stock in the middle of the night without my permission

takeaways.technique: Delegation claim distinguishing agent from user
takeaways.what_they_do: Access tokens carry an authorized-party claim identifying the agent acting on behalf of a subject, so policy and audit can attribute actions to the specific agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your access token will have an author authorizing party that's a claim identify not not the user but who is who the user is delegating the access to

takeaways.technique: Central token vault with refresh handling
takeaways.what_they_do: A vault stores upstream refresh tokens and mints short-lived access tokens on demand, so agents stay authenticated without re-prompting and without holding long-lived secrets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we take care of this nasty complex part of refreshing tokens, storing tokens
